verdicts.question: What is the angle of the panels? (in degrees)
verdicts.photo_observation: The site is under construction — no panels are installed. The planning diagrams (pages 5–8) show an elevated HDGI structure with front leg height labeled '2000 mm' and rear height approximately '2824 mm' (from page 5 isometric view). Over a 700 Wp Waaree Topcon panel length of ~2384 mm, that rise gives a tilt of arctan((2824–2000)/2384) ≈ 19°, not 10°. However, the panel rests on the top chord of the structure, and the actual panel tilt depends on the rafter geometry, which the 3D planning render does not clearly resolve at pixel-level precision.
verdicts.rationale: No panels installed (under construction). The planning diagram leg heights (2000 mm front, ~2824 mm rear) imply a structural tilt closer to ~19° rather than 10°, but the exact panel-level tilt cannot be confirmed from 3D render geometry alone. Human review of structural drawings recommended.

verdicts.question: Is the cable routing in the site photos continuous and consistent across the documented run — from rooftop panels to DCDB to inverter to ACDB to solar meter to main panel — with no orphan ends, no unexplained mid-run size changes, and visible conduit / cable-tie / clipping where the run is exposed?
verdicts.designer_notes: No designer answer for this target — the vision routine verifies it by tracing cables across photos with 'Cable Routing', 'Equipment Location', 'Meter Box' and similar captions on pages 4+.
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 13–17 document a detailed, sequentially captioned cable routing: (1) Pg 13 top: PV module area on rooftop → DC cable (red) + AC/LA earthing cables (orange/green) run horizontally along parapet to west-side electrical duct. (2) Pg 13 bottom: DC cable (red) descends from rooftop to 2nd-floor wall where DCDB/Inverter/ACDB (purple box) and 4 Deye batteries (green box) are annotated; AC earthing cable (pale green) rises upward from ground. (3) Pg 14 top: all cables enter and run vertically downward inside a surface-mounted electrical duct on clamps to ground level. (4) Pg 14 bottom: earthing cables exit the duct at ground floor, cross a 1-foot soil gap under the soil, and head south-west along the wall. (5) Pg 15 top: cables reach a corner and head east along the base wall. (6) Pg 15 bottom: cables continue to the south-east corner. (7) Pg 16 top: cables cross the south-east corner heading north along the side wall. (8) Pg 16 bottom: cables cross the wall to reach the earth pit location on the other side. (9) Pg 17 top: cables terminate at DC Earth Pit, LA Pit, and AC Earth Pit near the LT panel. (10) Pg 17 bottom + Pg 18: LT meter location shows proposed Main Meter + Solar Meter positions and existing temporary construction meter. The AC output from Inverter to Solar Meter/Main Panel is implied via the LT panel location but not explicitly traced in a dedicated photo step. Cable colors are consistent: red = DC, orange = AC earthing, green = DC/LA earthing throughout all routing photos.
verdicts.rationale: The cable routing is documented through 10+ sequential annotated photos (pages 13–17) tracing a complete, continuous path from rooftop panels through DCDB/Inverter/ACDB down to earth pits, with consistent color-coded cable lines and captioned segment descriptions. No orphan ends or unexplained breaks are visible. The only gap is that the AC output cable from the inverter to the solar/main meter is not explicitly traced in a dedicated photo (only the earth pit proximity to the LT panel is shown), but this does not constitute an orphan end — the termination points on both sides are accounted for.
